title: Beef Massaman Curry

extendedIngredients.name: beef chuck steak
extendedIngredients.original: 1 kg beef chuck steak, cut into 4 cm chunks

extendedIngredients.name: potatoes
extendedIngredients.original: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks

extendedIngredients.name: brown onion
extendedIngredients.original: 2 brown onions, cut into thick wedges

extendedIngredients.name: roasted peanuts
extendedIngredients.original: 75 g roasted peanuts, roughly chopped (about 1/2 cup)

steps: Cut the beef chuck steak into 4 cm chunks and season with salt. Heat a splash of oil in a large heavy pot over high heat and brown the beef in two batches. Set the beef aside.
Drop the heat to medium. Add the massaman curry paste and a few spoonfuls of the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk. Fry for 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Return the beef to the pot with the rest of the coconut milk, 250 ml water, the fish sauce, brown sugar, tamarind paste, cinnamon stick and star anise. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, stirring now and then so nothing catches on the bottom.

Add the potatoes and onion wedges. Simmer uncovered for another 45 minutes, until the beef pulls apart easily and the potatoes are tender. The sauce thickens on its own as it reduces and the potatoes soften.
While the curry finishes, rinse the jasmine rice and cook it by absorption or per the packet.
Fish out the cinnamon stick and star anise. Taste the curry and balance it with a little extra fish sauce or brown sugar if it needs it.
Serve the curry over the rice, topped with the chopped roasted peanuts and coriander leaves.
